summary: Incorrect RKHS-to-coefficient objective conversion and an exact failure of the central confidence-proof curvature inequality; fitted-weight concentration also unjustified.

problems.title: Representer conversion changes regularizer
problems.claim: RKHS penalty becomes Euclidean norm of kernel-section coefficients.
problems.check: Reproducing identity gives norm squared theta^T K theta. One-duel K4 example yields different strictly convex minimizers.

problems.counterevidence: Euclidean penalty would be valid in orthonormal feature coordinates, not the stated kernel-section expansion. K=I is a valid special case.
problems.impact: Disconnects specified estimator, proof, implemented algorithm; core confidence/regret claim depends on estimator.

correction.statement: Use lambda theta^T K theta/2 with consistent summed/mean loss scaling; full algorithm/theory repair unverified.
